messages.author: a305e65fa9dfb74d
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] multiple membership/cross classified models?
parts:
Dear Amit-
If my Google is not misleading, then a multiple membership model is a case where each sample can belong to several hierarchal classes at once; Say a neighborhood, within a city and a class within a school. While this structure might create nasty computations, I still seems to fit nicely in the framework of mixed models. You would have a school effect, a class effect, a neighborhood effect and a city effect. Each might be fixed or random. I guess this is why people suggest using the lmer function, and I tend to agree.
Having no experience with this type multiple membership models, I cannot add to what Google has to offer. 
On the lmer function of the lme4 package, I can say this: you should usually look for a vignette when learning a new package. In the case of lme4, the three available vignettes are very technical. Luckily, Doug Bates did a rather nice documentation job, which you can find here. I hope this helps.

J
